newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian interest payments to exceed fiscal deficit.
newsitem.headline: Indian interest payments to exceed fiscal deficit.

text.p: India could be heading for a debt trap with interest payments exceeding the government projected borrowings in 1997/98 (April-March) according to an independent research firm.

"Interest payments of 680 billion rupees during 1997/98 would exceed gross fiscal deficit, or net additions to borrowings of 654.54 billion for the year, by 45.46 billion," the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said in a report made available to Reuters on Monday.

Gross fiscal deficit (budget deficit plus government borrowings) for 1997/98 (April-March) was pegged at 654.54 billion rupees by finance minister P. Chidambaram in his budget presented to the Indian Parliament on February 28.
The 1997/98 budget provision for interest payments were higher by 95 billion rupees at 680 billion, CMIE said.

"When viewed against a rise of just around 23 billion rupees during the year, the 95 billion rupee rise in interest paymnets would imply that average cost of fresh borrowings including rollover of past loans has increased significantly," it said.
Interest payments will account for 29.3 percent of all government spending in 1997/98 according to budget estimates.
Of the government's borrowings, 46.2 percent went towards interest payments in 1988/89. This rose to 92.6 percent in 1996/97 and is expected to go up to 103.9 percent in 1997/98, CMIE said.
